confound_disclosed: F2 and F4 pass on the pre-registered comparisons, but the 2x2 control shows the gain is attributable to PREPAYMENT, not participation: holding distribution policy fixed, equity is worse than debt in both columns. Thresholds not moved, gates not re-scored, confound recorded.

gates.detail:
max unbacked claims 0.000e+00; invariant violations — corrected arm 0, fixed-debt arm 11
        *** The CORRECTED architecture holds full reserve exactly. The FIXED-DEBT comparator
        does not: after a shortfall its residual claim survives with no reserve behind it,
        which is what an unbacked debt IS. The gate says 'in every arm', so it FAILS as
        written — and the reason is a property of debt, not a bug in the build.

equity 94.4 vs fixed debt 2465.0  -> 96.2% reduction (needs >= 20%)
        promised  equity 91297.6 / debt 92197.6   delivered  equity 98685.2 / debt 89732.5

        *** DISCLOSURE — THIS PASS IS ENTIRELY ATTRIBUTABLE TO PREPAYMENT, NOT PARTICIPATION.
        The 2x2 control holds the distribution policy fixed and the ranking INVERTS:
            prepay ON    equity 94.4   vs   fixed debt 16.1
            prepay OFF   equity 4059.3   vs   fixed debt 2465.0
        In BOTH columns equity is WORSE than debt. The operative ingredient is the
        discipline of distributing inflows continuously, which is orthogonal to whether
        the claim is fixed or variable. Mechanism: writing a claim down EXTINGUISHES it,
        so the holder can never be made whole from later inflows, whereas a residual debt
        survives and is recoverable. The threshold is NOT moved and the gate is NOT
        re-scored, but the architecture's central innovation is not what is working.

secondary (knock-on) failures: equity 121 vs debt 190 -> 36.3% reduction (needs >= 30%)
        *** THIS IS THE ONE GATE THAT SURVIVES THE 2x2 CONTROL. Holding the
        distribution policy fixed, participation reduces cascade in BOTH columns:
            prepay ON    equity 121 vs debt 148  (18.2% fewer)
            prepay OFF   equity 129 vs debt 190  (32.1% fewer)
        So participation IS a real mechanism — but a CONTAGION control, not a
        loss reducer. Absorbing a loss without a hard default event genuinely
        stops it propagating; it does not make the loss smaller. Note the effect
        weakens to 18.2% once prepayment is present, below this gate's own threshold.

corrected 94.4 vs central full-reserve book 2184.4 (needs <= 2730.5); ratio 0.04x
        *** DISCLOSURE: the central comparator does NOT prepay. Given the same
        distribution discipline it scores 1105.7 — so this gate compares distribution
        policies, not topologies. On equal terms the central book is behind.

at k=20 there are 10 clusters so 1/K = 0.1000 (the proposal quoted 0.0100, which
        conflates cluster COUNT with cluster SIZE). MEASURED fraction of the network
        whose delivered value is impaired: 0.9350 — 9.3x the claimed quarantine.
        Damage is NOT confined to one cluster.

removing each component changes claimant shortfall by: full_reserve +8093.1  local_pooling +191.6  equity_participation -78.3  latency_covenant +125.9

        *** WORSE THAN DEAD WEIGHT — removing these IMPROVED the outcome: ['equity_participation']
        The equity ablation holds prepayment ON, so it isolates participation itself.
